summary: Riley Wood, writing in The Eyeopener (Toronto Metropolitan University's student newspaper) on July 1, 2016, argues against a conventional 'trans narrative' and describes their own experience as a tomboyish trans woman who enjoyed masculine pursuits. After reading Julia Serano's Whipping Girl, they realized tomboyish trans women are valid and began transitioning. The piece addresses misgendering, the pressure on trans women to exaggerate femininity, and the idea that clothing has no gender. Reader comments from 2017 to 2024 largely express relief at finding similar experiences.
one_line: A Toronto student writer describes being a tomboyish trans woman who rejected the stereotypical trans narrative after reading Julia Serano.
key_facts: The article was posted on July 1, 2016 by Eyeopener Staff and written by Riley Wood.
The Eyeopener is Toronto Metropolitan University's independent student newspaper, published since 1967.
The author describes a conventional 'trans narrative' with themes such as 'I always played with dolls, never cars' and 'I just knew.'
As a child the author played with cars, rode dirt bikes, rough housed, and played video games.
The author's therapist suspected clinical depression before the author understood their gender feelings.
The author attended a support group called Trans Youth Toronto, which is described as discontinued.
The author read Julia Serano's Whipping Girl for a sex and gender studies course, which prompted them to start transitioning.
Julia Serano describes herself as a woman who 'rarely wears makeup, who regularly dresses like a tomboy.'
The author states that 'Clothing does not belong to any gender, even if it does play a role in how you may express it.'
The author says that for many trans women, highlighting and exaggerating femininity is a requirement for being taken seriously.
The author writes that 'you don't have to be sure to be trans or transition.'
A commenter named Jamie wrote that they were 17 months into transition and had been on hormones for 14 months.
Comments on the article are dated from August 21, 2017 to January 24, 2024.
